I'm checking whether `import-reachability` is a real package; PyPI has nothing by that name, so I'm reading the code_facts sources to confirm it's an internal stage name.## import-reachability

### What it is
`import-reachability` is not a third-party package. Nobody publishes it: `https://pypi.org/pypi/import-reachability/json` and `.../import_reachability/json` both returned HTTP 404 on 2026-10-17. It is the name of an internal pre-filter stage in this change (D10, and the `import_reachability` drop stage in D11). The new `plugins/multiplai-dev/lib/code_facts/code_facts/pyindex.py` builds a static import graph with the standard library's `ast`, then runs a reverse breadth-first search from the changed `.py` files. Any entry whose handler module (or location module) cannot reach a changed file is dropped as `unreachable` before any `CallFn` call. The dependency detector flagged it by mistake, and its reason is itself wrong. It says "0 declared name(s) scanned", but `lib/code_facts/pyproject.toml` declares `multiplai-core[sdk]` and `pydantic>=2`, so the scanner probably read a different pyproject. What this stage really depends on is CPython's `ast` parser, `os.scandir` and `pathlib` on the interpreter `uv` picks (`requires-python = ">=3.12"`). Its correctness is entirely our own code, so this section treats the stage as the dependency.

### The contract we rely on
Standard-library calls, quoted verbatim from the [3.12 `ast` docs](https://docs.python.org/3.12/library/ast.html) and the [`compile()` docs](https://docs.python.org/3.12/library/functions.html):
- `ast.parse(source, filename='<unknown>', mode='exec', *, type_comments=False, feature_version=None)`: "Parse the source into an AST node. Equivalent to `compile(source, filename, mode, ast.PyCF_ONLY_AST)`."
- `class ast.ImportFrom(module, names, level)`, with grammar `ImportFrom(identifier? module, alias* names, int? level)`. The docs say: "`module` is a raw string of the 'from' name, without any leading dots, or `None` for statements such as `from . import foo`. `level` is an integer holding the level of the relative import (0 means absolute import)."
- `ast.Import(names)` gives one `alias` per dotted name.
- `compile()`: "raises `SyntaxError` if the compiled source is invalid, and `ValueError` if the source contains null bytes." The docs also warn: "It is possible to crash the Python interpreter with a sufficiently large/complex string when compiling to an AST object due to stack depth limitations in Python's AST compiler."
- `feature_version`: "'Best-effort' … no guarantee that the parse (or success of the parse) is the same as when run on the Python version corresponding to `feature_version`". The highest allowed value is the running interpreter's version.

Internal contract that the design promises (D4, D10, D11):
- The stage runs only when `changed_lines is not None`. Changed `.py` files are the BFS seeds.
- An entry's distance is 0 if its location file changed. Otherwise it is the BFS distance of its handler module, or of its location module when there is no handler and the location is a `.py` file. `None` means a `DropRecord(stage="import_reachability", reason="unreachable")`.
- Edges come from `Import` and `ImportFrom`, including relative imports, `from . import b` and package `__init__`.
- Unparseable modules have no out-edges. Unresolved imports add no edges. Cycles terminate.
- Resolution never crosses into another repository in the snapshot.
- A parse failure is caught only as `SyntaxError` or `UnicodeDecodeError`, and becomes a `parse_error` diagnostic with `line=None`.
- Survivors are ordered by `(distance, KIND_RANK, path, line)` before `trace_limit` is applied.

### Edge cases & failure modes
- **Empty scope (`changed_lines == {}`).** Following D10 as written: there are no seeds and no location file changed, so every entry gets distance `None`. All E entries are dropped at `import_reachability`, with 0 paths and 0 trace calls, and the fallback is `skipped/empty_scope`. There is no error and no warning that the run did nothing. `changed_lines=None` skips the stage entirely and drops nothing.
- **A changed file with an empty line list (`{"a.py": []}`).** Unknown: does a key with no lines count as a changed file, making it a seed and putting entries in that file at distance 0? Check with a fixture. If it does, those entries are traced (real `CallFn` cost) and then all dropped at `no_changed_line`, because coverage is empty.
- **Only non-`.py` files changed** (`SKILL.md`, `hooks.json`, `pyproject.toml`, a JSON or YAML file a handler `open()`s). There are no BFS seeds. Only entries whose location is that exact file survive. A handler that reads a changed data file at runtime is dropped as `unreachable`, which is a false negative.
- **Deleted `.py` file.** The file isn't in the snapshot index, so it can't be a seed. Its unchanged importers (which now break at runtime) are dropped as `unreachable`. The design only says "a missing file is tolerated".
- **Null bytes.** The docs say `ValueError`, but on 3.12 the parser actually raises `SyntaxError: source code string cannot contain null bytes`. This changed in gh-96670 ([What's New 3.12](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/4d5fcca273b24a5566f1507758e5aae60cdf8a98/Doc/whatsnew/3.12.rst); it [broke pyflakes' build](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2175154)). The `SyntaxError | UnicodeDecodeError` catch therefore covers it, but only because the docs are out of date.
- **UTF-8 BOM or a PEP 263 coding cookie.** If a file is read with `read_text("utf-8")` and the `str` is passed to `ast.parse`, a leading `\ufeff` makes the parse fail with `SyntaxError` (invalid non-printable character U+FEFF), and a latin-1 file with a `# -*- coding: latin-1 -*-` cookie fails with `UnicodeDecodeError`. Passing `bytes` respects both. Which one D4 does is unspecified.
- **Syntax newer than the interpreter.** For example PEP 758 `except A, B:` (3.14) or t-strings (3.14) parsed under 3.12, or Python 2 files. These give `SyntaxError`, so the module has no out-edges. The catch: when that module imports a changed module, entries handled in it are dropped as `unreachable`, which looks like a scope decision. A separate `parse_error` diagnostic is the only clue.
- **Implicit package execution.** `import a.b.c` runs `a/__init__.py` and `a/b/__init__.py`, and `python -m pkg` runs `pkg/__init__.py` before `pkg/__main__.py`. Unknown: does the graph add edges to parent `__init__.py` files? If not, a change to `a/__init__.py` makes importers of `a.b.c` unreachable. Check with a fixture.
- **`from . import x`** (`module=None`, `level=1`). `x` may be a submodule (`x.py`) or a name defined in `__init__.py`. Resolving to only one of the two either misses edges or adds spurious ones. `from ... import y` past the top of the package or repository must resolve to nothing, not to a path outside the repo.
- **Dynamic and indirect imports.** `importlib.import_module(...)`, `__import__`, entry-point plugins, `sys.path.insert(...)` followed by `import` (this repo's convention in `scripts/`), `runpy`, and `subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", ...])` create no edges. Code reached only that way is dropped as `unreachable`.
- **Over-inclusion.** Imports under `if TYPE_CHECKING:`, in `try/except ImportError` fallbacks, and in functions that never run all create edges. Entries get traced that can't really reach the change. That costs `CallFn` calls, then the entry falls to `no_changed_line`. `from m import *` gives only an edge to `m`.
- **Multi-repo snapshot.** "Never crosses repos" means a repo that imports a sibling repo checked out in the same snapshot (for example `multiplai_core` next to `multiplai-dev`) gets no edge. Changes in the sibling repo make the dependent entries unreachable.
- **Symlinked modules.** Symlinks whose `resolve()` points outside `root` are not followed, so imports satisfied only through them are unresolved and add no edge.
- **Oversized input.** There is no file-count, size or time limit. The whole snapshot is walked and parsed whatever the scope. Deeply nested or very long expressions (generated code, long `+` chains, huge literals) can raise `RecursionError` or `MemoryError`, or crash the interpreter, according to the docs. On 3.12+, CPython [added C-stack protection that surfaces as `RecursionError: Stack overflow`](https://chromium.googlesource.com/external/github.com/python/cpython/+show/03503dccd0aa6d8895614e80ae9c78c03c813d45/InternalDocs/stack_protection.md), and [3.12's recursion limits for `ast.parse` were reported as low](https://discuss.python.org/t/recursion-limits/33869). Neither exception is in the catch list, so one such file aborts the whole `map_paths` call. Unknown: which exception 3.12 and 3.13 actually raise on Linux and macOS for each shape. See the experiment below.
- **Concurrent or repeated use.** The walk and parse are synchronous CPU work inside `async map_paths`, so they block the event loop for the full parse, and concurrent `map_paths` calls run one after another. `os.scandir` order is arbitrary; the design sorts names, which keeps BFS distances stable. Unknown: is the `ast` parse cache module-level and keyed by path? If so, a second run on a reused `tmp_path` with different contents gets stale trees. Check by running `map_paths` twice in one process on a mutated fixture.
- **Offline, unavailable, unauthenticated.** The stage makes no network calls and needs no auth, so it works offline. The real mismatch is about the source of the bytes. Reachability reads the working tree with `os.scandir`, while the gate reads `git show <sha>:<rel>` through `resolve`. A dirty tree, untracked `.py` files, a sparse checkout or LFS pointer files mean distances are computed on different bytes from the ones traced and cited.
- **Unreadable files.** Unknown: does a `PermissionError` or `IsADirectoryError` on a `.py` path (for example a directory named `x.py`) crash the run, given that only `SyntaxError | UnicodeDecodeError` are caught? Check with a `chmod 000` fixture.

### Assumptions we are making
- `import-reachability` adds nothing to `pyproject.toml` or `uv.lock`. No package by that name is installed or imported.
- On every interpreter `uv` selects for code_facts, `ast.parse` raises `SyntaxError` (not `ValueError`) for source containing `\0`.
- Files are passed to `ast.parse` as `bytes`, so a UTF-8 BOM and PEP 263 cookies parse without a `parse_error`.
- Every `.py` file under this repository's plugin trees parses under the selected interpreter, giving 0 `parse_error` diagnostics on the live repo.
- `ast.parse` on a pathologically nested but valid file raises a Python exception (it does not segfault), and that exception is caught and turned into `parse_error` rather than aborting `map_paths`.
- Importing `a.b.c` puts edges to `a/__init__.py` and `a/b/__init__.py` in the graph, so changing either gives a finite distance for importers of `a.b.c`.
- `from . import x` resolves to `x.py` (or `x/__init__.py`) when that exists, and to the package's `__init__.py` otherwise.
- For every entry handler in this repo, every module it reaches at runtime is also reachable through static `import` / `from … import` edges. No handler reaches project code only through `importlib`, `sys.path` changes, `runpy` or a subprocess.
- For every `.py` file, the snapshot's working-tree bytes equal `git show <commit>:<rel>`.
- Walking and parsing this whole repository takes under 2 seconds and under 200 MB of RSS, so no limit is needed.
- Two `map_paths` calls in one process on the same path with different contents give distances computed from the current contents.
- With `changed_lines == {}`, the result has 0 paths and every entry dropped at `import_reachability`. This is the intended behaviour, not a bug for callers to guard against.

### How we would find out cheaply
1. **No package.** `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://pypi.org/pypi/import-reachability/json` should print `404` (it did on 2026-10-17), and `rg -n 'import.reachability' uv.lock '**/pyproject.toml'` should find nothing. Any hit disproves the first assumption.
2. **Parser behaviour** (save outside any snapshot, run with `uv run --directory plugins/multiplai-dev/lib/code_facts python -I probe.py`):
   ```python
   import ast, sys
   for label, src in [("nul", "x=1\0"), ("bom-str", "\ufeffx=1"), ("bom-bytes", b"\xef\xbb\xbfx=1"),
                      ("unary", "-"*200000+"1"), ("chain", "1"+"+1"*200000), ("nest", "["*5000+"]"*5000)]:
       try: ast.parse(src); print(label, "ok")
       except BaseException as e: print(label, type(e).__name__, str(e)[:60])
   print(sys.version)
   ```
   `nul → ValueError` disproves the null-byte assumption. `bom-bytes` failing disproves the bytes assumption. Exit code 139 (segfault), or `RecursionError` / `MemoryError` on any of the last three, disproves the "caught as `parse_error`" assumption unless the catch list is widened. Run it on macOS too, since stack sizes differ.
3. **Live-repo parse and timing.** Use a 10-line script that walks the repo with D4's exclusions, `ast.parse`s each `.py` file as bytes, counts failures and prints the elapsed time (`/usr/bin/time -v` for peak RSS). Any failure disproves "every file parses". More than 2 s or 200 MB disproves the size assumption.
4. **Dynamic-import audit.** `rg -n 'importlib\.import_module|__import__\(|sys\.path\.(insert|append)|runpy\.|subprocess\.(run|call|check_|Popen)' --type py plugins/`. Any hit inside a discovered handler's transitive import closure that reaches project code disproves the static-superset assumption, and marks a place where a real path gets dropped as `unreachable`.
5. **Graph fixtures** (three pytest cases in `tests/fixtures/paths/`):
   - `pkg/__init__.py` changed, with the handler doing `import pkg.sub`: expect distance 1, and `None` disproves the parent-`__init__` assumption;
   - `from . import x`, with `x.py` present and then absent: expect edges to `x.py` and then `__init__.py`;
   - `changed_lines={}`: expect `len(paths)==0`, every drop at `import_reachability`, and `FakeCall.calls == 0`.
6. **Tree versus commit.** In the snapshot, `git status --porcelain -- '*.py'` should print nothing. Any line disproves the bytes-equal-commit assumption for that run.
7. **Stale cache.** Call `discover_entries` and `map_paths` on a fixture, rewrite the handler module to drop its import of the changed file, then call again in the same process. If the distance is unchanged, the cache is stale.

## invocation

### What it is
`invocation` is not a third-party dependency. Nobody maintains it as a package, and there is nothing to install. On 2026-10-17, both `https://pypi.org/pypi/invocation/json` and `https://pypi.org/simple/invocation/` returned **HTTP 404**, so no package with this name exists on PyPI. The scanner picked it up because design.md uses the word as a code-formatted identifier in two places. D13 says "The `Entry` object likewise carries `handler`, `invocation`, `known_edges` and `source`". D8 says "Repository text quoted in the prompt (`invocation` strings, hook commands) is wrapped with `multiplai_core.untrusted.fence`". In this change, `invocation` is a field on the new `Entry` output model in `paths.py`. It holds the literal text a user or harness runs to reach an entry point: a `SKILL.md` shell line, a `hooks.json` command string, a `[project.scripts]` key, or an argparse/click subcommand path. It flows into four places: `paths.json`, the `trace_entry` prompt (fenced as untrusted), the e2e `subprocess` matcher (D12), and the hook-command matching that uses `shlex`. The rest of this section treats it as an internal contract, because the behavior that matters comes from the stdlib calls that produce and consume it. The project tree was not available to inspect: the working directory is empty and `plugins/multiplai-dev/lib/code_facts/` was not found. So everything about existing code_facts behavior below comes from design.md, not from reading code.

### The contract we rely on
- **Nothing external.** No import, no install, no `pyproject.toml` entry. **Action: do not run `uv add invocation`.** The name is unclaimed on PyPI, so anyone could register it later. Adding it would give you an attacker-controlled package under a name that looks plausible.
- **Internal field (as the design implies, but does not specify):** `Entry.invocation` on a `_Strict(_Model)` (`extra="forbid"`) output model, serialised by `write_paths_file` with `model_dump(mode="json")` and then `json.dumps(indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n"`. Its type, whether it can be null, and its per-kind format are **not stated anywhere** in design.md D1–D14.
- **Stdlib calls that produce or consume it**, as documented:
  - `shlex.split(s, comments=False, posix=True)`: "Split the string *s* using shell-like syntax." Used for `SKILL.md` lines (D4) and for hook commands in the `subprocess` matcher (D12).
  - `json.loads(s)` on `hooks.json` and `.claude/settings*.json`. The source line is then found by "scanning the raw text for the JSON-encoded string" (D4), which implies something like `json.dumps(cmd)` searched with `str.find`.
  - `tomllib.loads(s)` for `[project.scripts]`. `tomllib` gives no line positions, so a line scan supplies them.
  - `multiplai_core.untrusted.fence(text)`: a project-internal helper whose signature and escaping behavior this research could not confirm.

### Edge cases & failure modes
- **Empty or degenerate input:** `shlex.split("")` and `shlex.split("   ")` return `[]`, not an error. An empty hook `"command": ""` or a blank continuation-joined `SKILL.md` line therefore yields zero tokens. The `python -m` matcher silently fails to match, so you get no entry and no diagnostic, unless the scanner emits one explicitly. D4's "each skipped candidate produces exactly one diagnostic" covers only *candidates*, and it is unclear whether an empty command counts as one.
- **Malformed input:**
  - An unbalanced quote makes `shlex.split` raise `ValueError: No closing quotation`. The design names no diagnostic reason for it (`parse_error`? `dynamic_name`?). Unless that exception is caught, it propagates out of `discover_entries`.
  - With the default `punctuation_chars=False`, `shlex.split("cd x&&python3 -m m")` returns `['cd', 'x&&python3', '-m', 'm']`. The `cd <dir> &&` prefix rule (D4) misses this because `&&` is not a separate token. Likewise `;` and `|` stay glued to their neighbours.
  - `shlex` does not expand `$VAR`. D4 expands `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}` and `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` itself; every other variable reaches the matcher as a literal `$X` token.
- **JSON line lookup:**
  - `json.dumps` defaults to `ensure_ascii=True` and never emits `\/`. A hook file that writes `"\/usr\/bin"`, uses `\u` escapes differently, or contains raw non-ASCII will not contain the re-encoded string. The line lookup then fails even though `json.loads` parsed the file. That leaves the entry with no line, but `line ≥ 1` is a model invariant (D13).
  - Duplicate identical commands depend on the "occurrences in document order" rule. A key-order mismatch (for example, a `matcher` key whose value equals a command) would shift the assignment.
- **Oversized input:** no length limit is specified for `invocation`. Hook commands are often inline `python -c "…"` or `bash -c` scripts several KB long. They would be quoted whole into every `trace_entry` prompt, and again into `retrace_entry`, with no truncation, unlike the 200-character error convention in D5.
- **Cache key:** the D7 trace key is `(kind, location, handler)` plus ranges, edges and places, and **does not include `invocation`**. Editing a command string in place (same line, same handler) reuses the cached trace answer, even though the prompt text would now differ.
- **Concurrent or repeated use:** the field is an immutable `str` with no shared state, so it is thread-safe. The open question is repeated invocations of one handler. The D4 merge keeps one entry and moves the rest into `also_invoked_by`, and D12 matches "the entry and every `also_invoked_by` invoker". The design does not say whether `also_invoked_by` records carry their own `invocation`. If they do not, the `subprocess` matcher cannot match the losing invokers' command strings.
- **Offline / unavailable / unauthenticated:** nothing is fetched at runtime, so nothing can fail offline. The only offline failure is self-inflicted: if someone runs `uv add invocation`, resolution fails with a "not found in the package registry" error. That fails loudly, which is the good case. The bad case is that it succeeds later, after someone registers the name.
- **Unknown:** does `multiplai_core.untrusted.fence` escape or neutralise a fence delimiter that appears *inside* the quoted text (for example, a `SKILL.md` line containing the fence marker)? To check, call `fence("x <END> y")`, using the real delimiter, and inspect the output.
- **Unknown:** what does `invocation` hold for non-shell kinds (`argparse_subcommand`, `click_command`, `main_module`, `seed`, `other`): `None`, `"prog sub"`, or `"python -m pkg sub"`? To check, read the `Entry` model once PR 1 adds it. Today the design is silent.

### Assumptions we are making
- `invocation` refers only to the internal `Entry.invocation` field, and no code anywhere does `import invocation`. This is false if `rg -n '^\s*(import|from)\s+invocation\b'` matches anything.
- Every hook command that `json.loads` parses can be located by searching the raw file text for `json.dumps(cmd)`. This is false for any file that contains `\/` or raw non-ASCII inside a command.
- `shlex.split` never raises on `SKILL.md` and hook content in this repository. This is false if any fenced shell block or hook command has an unbalanced quote.
- Commands of the form `cd <dir> && python -m …` are always written with spaces around `&&`. This is false if any `SKILL.md` or hooks file contains `&&` touching a non-space character.
- Changing `invocation` without changing location or handler does not need a fresh trace. This is false if the trace answer cites the command text, because it would then go stale under the D7 key.
- `invocation` strings are short enough to quote in full in prompts. This is false if any hook command in the repository is longer than about 2 KB.
- The name `invocation` is still unregistered on PyPI. This is false if `curl -so /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://pypi.org/pypi/invocation/json` returns `200`.

### How we would find out cheaply
Run this from the repository root (Python 3.11+, stdlib only). Each `print` line maps to one assumption.

```python
import json, pathlib, shlex, re
root = pathlib.Path(".")
print("imports:", [str(p) for p in root.rglob("*.py") if re.search(r"^\s*(import|from)\s+invocation\b", p.read_text("utf-8", "ignore"), re.M)])  # non-empty -> assumption 1 false
print(shlex.split(""), shlex.split("cd x&&python3 -m m"))  # [] and ['cd','x&&python3',...] confirm the empty/glued-&& behaviour
for f in [*root.rglob("hooks.json"), *root.rglob(".claude/settings*.json")]:
    raw = f.read_text("utf-8"); data = json.loads(raw)
    for ev in data.get("hooks", {}).values():
        for grp in ev:
            for h in grp.get("hooks", []):
                c = h.get("command", "")
                if json.dumps(c) not in raw: print("UNLOCATABLE", f, c[:60])      # assumption 2 false
                try: shlex.split(c)
                except ValueError as e: print("SHLEX", f, e)                     # assumption 3 false
                if re.search(r"\S&&|&&\S", c): print("GLUED &&", f)              # assumption 4 false
                if len(c) > 2048: print("LONG", f, len(c))                       # assumption 6 false
```

Next, run `rg -n '\S&&|&&\S' -g 'SKILL.md'` to check the `SKILL.md` side of assumption 4. Run `curl -so /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://pypi.org/pypi/invocation/json`: anything other than `404` falsifies assumption 7. Finally, add one test that edits only a hook's command text, re-runs `map_paths` with the same `cache_dir`, and asserts the `CallFn` call count. A count of 0 confirms the stale-cache case behind assumption 5.

## invocation-line

### What it is
`invocation-line` is not a third-party dependency. Nothing by that name exists on PyPI (`https://pypi.org/pypi/invocation-line/json` returns HTTP 404), and the string `invocation_line` does not appear anywhere in this checkout. The dependency scanner probably picked up the hyphenated term from design.md § D12, where `invocation_line` is a field on each e2e test record (`node_id`, `file`, `line`, `match`, `invocation_line`, plus `patch_line` for mocks). The code that produces it, `code_facts/e2e.py`, is new and owned by this project. Under the hood, the "dependency" is CPython's standard-library `ast` module, specifically the `lineno` / `end_lineno` position attributes on `ast.Call` nodes, on the interpreter that `code_facts` requires (`requires-python = ">=3.12"` in `lib/code_facts/pyproject.toml`). In this change, `invocation_line` records the line of the call that makes a test end-to-end: a direct handler call, `main([...])`, `CliRunner().invoke(...)`, `subprocess.*` or `runpy.run_module`. It is also used to deduplicate each test to its earliest such line.

### The contract we rely on
- `ast.parse(source, filename='<unknown>', mode='exec', *, type_comments=False, feature_version=None, optimize=-1)` (3.13 signature; 3.12 has no `optimize`) returns an `ast.Module`. It raises `SyntaxError` on invalid source.
- `ast.Call` (like every `ast.expr` / `ast.stmt`) carries `lineno`, `col_offset`, `end_lineno` and `end_col_offset`. The docs say: "`lineno` and `end_lineno` are the first and last line numbers of source text span (1-indexed so the first line is line 1)". For a `Call`, the span starts where the **whole expression** starts, which is the callee expression, not the `(`.
- Since 3.8, `FunctionDef.lineno` / `ClassDef.lineno` is the `def` / `class` line, not the first decorator line. Each decorator is a separate node in `decorator_list` with its own `lineno`.
- Since 3.12 (PEP 701), expressions inside f-strings get real source positions.
- What design.md D12 promises for this field:
  - `invocation_line` is the line of the matched call node in the test body, with nested `def`s excluded.
  - Records are sorted by `(file, line, node_id)`.
  - Each test is deduplicated to its earliest `invocation_line`, then by match-kind order.
  - `patch_line` is the patch's own line, which may be in `conftest.py`.
  - `file` and the line refer to the file under `root` as read from disk (the e2e listing walks the filesystem; it does not use `git show`).

### Edge cases & failure modes
- **Empty or degenerate input:**
  - `ast.parse("")` returns `Module(body=[])`, so an empty `test_*.py` produces no records and no skip. The file silently disappears instead of being reported.
  - A test whose only call is `subprocess.run(cmd)`, where `cmd` is a variable, gets no `invocation_line` and is not listed. D12 matches only literal lists or strings, so a whole class of real e2e tests is silently missed.
- **Multi-line or chained calls (unexpected format):**
  - For `CliRunner()\n    .invoke(app, [...])` or `result = (runner\n .invoke(...))`, `Call.lineno` is the line where `runner` / `CliRunner()` starts, not the `.invoke` line.
  - For `subprocess.run(\n [sys.executable, "-m", ...])`, it is the `subprocess.run` line, not the line holding the argv.
  - A consumer that quotes "the line" will show text that may not contain the matched tokens.
- **Line counting differs between `ast` and `str.splitlines()`.** The CPython tokenizer ends lines only on `\n`, `\r\n` and `\r`. `str.splitlines()` also splits on `\x0c` (form feed, legal whitespace in Python source), `\x0b`, `\x1c`–`\x1e`, `\x85`, `\u2028` and `\u2029`. Any later code that looks up `invocation_line` with `text.splitlines()[n-1]` drifts by one line for every such character above the call.
- **Malformed input:**
  - A BOM in `str` input: if the file is decoded with `.read_text()` (not `utf-8-sig`) and the result passed to `ast.parse`, a leading U+FEFF raises `SyntaxError: invalid non-printable character U+FEFF`. The file is then skipped as `syntax_error`, although pytest runs it fine. Passing `bytes` avoids this, and also makes PEP 263 `# -*- coding: … -*-` cookies apply.
  - Null bytes: on 3.12, source containing `\x00` raises `SyntaxError` ("source code string cannot contain null bytes"). Through 3.11 it was `ValueError`. Recheck this if `requires-python` is ever lowered, because D12 catches only `SyntaxError` and the decode error.
- **Oversized or deeply nested input:**
  - More than 200 nested brackets raises `SyntaxError: too many nested parentheses`, which maps to `syntax_error`.
  - Very deep expression chains (e.g. generated `a+a+…` with ~100k terms) can raise `RecursionError` or `MemoryError` from `ast.parse`. Neither is caught by the D12 skip rules, so one generated test file aborts the whole `map_paths` run.
  - There is no size cap or timeout on `ast.parse`.
- **Concurrent or repeated use:**
  - `ast.parse` is a pure function with no global state, and it returns new node objects on every call, so re-parsing gives equal line numbers.
  - The shared parse cache in `pyindex` is plain in-process state. D8 runs traces under `bounded(concurrency)` on one event loop, and e2e listing is synchronous, so there is no observed race.
  - Unknown: whether listing ever runs in a thread pool, in which case concurrent cache fills duplicate work but stay deterministic. Check with a grep for `to_thread` / `run_in_executor` in the PR.
- **Disk/commit mismatch (the "unavailable" case):**
  - No network, auth or service is involved.
  - The real availability failure is that `invocation_line` comes from the working-tree file under `root`, while hop citations are verified with `git show <sha>:<rel>` (D9). If `root` has uncommitted edits or is not the checkout of `commit`, the line points at different text than the commit `paths.json` names, and nothing flags it.
  - A file removed between walk and parse raises `FileNotFoundError`, which is not a listed skip reason.
- **Parametrised and decorated tests:**
  - For `@pytest.mark.parametrize(...)` tests, one static record stands for N runtime pytest node ids (`test_x[a]`, `test_x[b]`). `invocation_line` is shared, and the static `node_id` matches none of pytest's ids exactly.
  - For decorator patches, `patch_line` is the decorator's line, which comes before the test's `def` line. So `patch_line < line` is normal, not a bug.

### Assumptions we are making
- On Python ≥3.12, `ast.Call.lineno` for `runner.invoke(...)` split over several lines equals the line where the receiver expression starts. It is never the `.invoke` line when the receiver sits on an earlier line.
- The same source text gives the same `invocation_line` on every supported CPython version (3.12, 3.13, 3.14).
- Every file `e2e.py` decodes is decoded so that a UTF-8 BOM does not turn a valid test into `syntax_error`.
- `ast.parse` on files under `root` raises only `SyntaxError` (including the null-byte case on 3.12+) or the decode error. It never raises `RecursionError`, `MemoryError` or `ValueError` on any file in this repository.
- Any consumer that turns `invocation_line` into text indexes lines the way the tokenizer does (`\n`, `\r\n`, `\r`), not with `str.splitlines()`.
- The file under `root` at listing time is byte-identical to `git show <commit>:<rel>` for every test file listed.
- "Earliest `invocation_line`" is well-defined because one test can match two kinds on the same line (e.g. `cli_argv` and `direct_call` on `main(["x"])`), and the match-kind tiebreak always picks the same one.

### How we would find out cheaply
Run this script once on each supported interpreter: `uv run --python 3.12 python -I probe.py`, then again with `--python 3.13` and `--python 3.14`. Keep `probe.py` in a scratch directory.

```python
import ast, sys
def first_call_line(src):
    return min(n.lineno for n in ast.walk(ast.parse(src)) if isinstance(n, ast.Call))
print(sys.version_info[:2])
print("chain", first_call_line("r = (runner\n    .invoke(app, ['x']))\n"))  # expect 1, falsified if 2
print("ff", first_call_line("a = 1\n\x0cmain(['x'])\n"), "\x0c".join(["a=1\n", "main(['x'])\n"]).splitlines().__len__())  # ast says 2; splitlines yields 3 lines -> drift
for name, src in [("bom", "\ufeffmain()\n"), ("nul", "main()\x00\n"), ("deep", "x=" + "+".join(["a"]*200000))]:
    try: ast.parse(src); print(name, "ok")
    except Exception as e: print(name, type(e).__name__, str(e)[:60])
```

How each result falsifies an assumption:
- **`chain`:** if it prints `2`, the receiver-line assumption is wrong. If the three interpreters print different values, the cross-version assumption is wrong.
- **`ff`:** if `ast` and `splitlines` disagree, any `splitlines`-based consumer is wrong.
- **`bom`:** if it prints `SyntaxError`, the decode path must use `utf-8-sig` or pass bytes.
- **`nul` and `deep`:** any exception type other than `SyntaxError` shows that D12's skip list is incomplete and that a single file can abort the run.

For the disk/commit assumption, run `git -C <root> status --porcelain -- '*test_*.py' '*_test.py'` before listing. Any output means `invocation_line` can disagree with `commit`. For the tiebreak assumption, add one fixture test containing `main(["sub"])` and check that the listing produces exactly one record with a stable `match` across 20 runs, using `pytest -p no:randomly --count=20` if pytest-repeat is available.

## kind

### What it is
`kind` is not a dependency. In the design, "kind" is a field name: D3 defines a project-local `EntryKind` enum (`argparse_subcommand`, `click_command`, `typer_command`, `main_module`, `project_script`, `skill_command`, `hook_command`, `seed`, `other`) and a `KIND_RANK` precedence list. The dependency scanner read the "Kind vocabulary" heading and the `kind` field as a package name. I checked whether anything called `kind` could be meant:
- **PyPI:** there is no Python distribution called `kind`. `https://pypi.org/pypi/kind/json` and `https://pypi.org/simple/kind/` both return HTTP 404.
- **The Kubernetes `kind` tool:** this is a Go CLI that runs Kubernetes clusters in Docker, maintained by Kubernetes SIGs. Nothing in D1–D14 starts clusters, containers or subprocesses. D14 actually adds a guard test that makes `subprocess.Popen` and `os.system` raise during discovery.
- **The existing code:** `code_facts/code_facts/` contains no `import kind`, `from kind` or any use of the identifier `kind`.

The scanner note "0 declared name(s) scanned" is also wrong for this package. `plugins/multiplai-dev/lib/code_facts/pyproject.toml` declares `multiplai-core[sdk]` and `pydantic>=2`, so the scanner probably read a different or empty `pyproject.toml`. The dependency this change really adds is `jsonschema>=4` (D13), and that is the one that needs an explainer.

### The contract we rely on
- **No third-party API is called.** The "contract" is a project-defined type that the change will write:
  - `EntryKind`: a closed enum with exactly the nine values above, used in the models, the generated schema and `paths.json`.
  - `KIND_RANK`: the discovery precedence order, with `other` last. It decides merge precedence, pre-trace order and output ordering (D3, D4, D10).
  - `FallbackEntry.kind: str`: free text from the model, normalised as "unknown `kind` becomes `other`" (D5).
- **Standard-library and existing modules the kind-related code uses:** `enum` (or a pydantic `Literal`/`StrEnum`) and pydantic v2 validation. Both are already available: `requires-python = ">=3.12"` and `pydantic>=2`.

### Edge cases & failure modes
- **Empty or degenerate input:** Unknown: what happens to a model fallback entry whose `kind` is `""` or whitespace? D5 says unknown kinds become `other`, but the normalisation code isn't written yet. Check with a unit test that passes `kind=""` and asserts `other`.
- **Malformed or unexpected-format input:** the spec's own fallback example uses kind `route`. Under D3 it is stored as `other` and the label goes into `name`, so the original kind label is lost from the `kind` field. Unknown: are case variants such as `"Argparse_Subcommand"` or `"argparse"` (the output contract's old short names) mapped to the enum, or collapsed to `other`? Check with a unit test over those strings.
- **Oversized input:** there is no `kind` package, so there are no size limits, truncation or timeouts. The only bound is the enum's nine values.
- **Concurrent or repeated use:** `EntryKind` and `KIND_RANK` are module-level constants with no state. The real risk is someone reordering `KIND_RANK`. That would silently change merge winners, output order and the cache keys that include `kind`, which would invalidate cached answers. D3 plans a test that pins the ranking.
- **Offline / unavailable / unauthenticated:** adding `kind` to `pyproject.toml` because of this report would make `uv lock` / `uv sync` fail. PyPI returns 404 for `kind`, so resolution would fail with "no solution found" or "not found in the package registry".
- **Scanner misdetection (observed):** the scanner reported "0 declared names" for a `pyproject.toml` that declares 2. The new-dependency check missed `jsonschema` (D13) and flagged `kind`. Other names it reports for this change shouldn't be trusted as-is.

### Assumptions we are making
- No Python distribution called `kind` exists on PyPI, so `pip download kind` / `uv pip install kind` fails.
- No module in `code_facts/` will `import kind` after this change. A grep for `^\s*(import|from)\s+kind\b` over the package finds nothing.
- The change never runs the Kubernetes `kind` binary. No `subprocess` call in the new modules has the string `"kind"` as `argv[0]`.
- `jsonschema>=4` is the only new third-party runtime dependency in the design. After the change, the `pyproject.toml` diff adds exactly one entry under `dependencies`.
- Every non-enum string the model returns as a kind is stored as `other`, and every value written to `paths.json` `kind` is one of the nine enum literals.

### How we would find out cheaply
1. **Is there a `kind` package on PyPI?** Run:
   ```
   curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://pypi.org/pypi/kind/json
   ```
   `404` confirms there isn't one (already observed). `200` falsifies the first assumption.
2. **Is anything importing it?** After implementation, run:
   ```
   rg -n '^\s*(import|from)\s+kind\b|\["kind"' plugins/multiplai-dev/lib/code_facts/code_facts
   ```
   Any import match falsifies the second assumption. Any `["kind", …]` argv falsifies the third.
3. **Does `kind` sneak into the dependency list?** Run:
   ```
   git diff -U0 -- plugins/multiplai-dev/lib/code_facts/pyproject.toml | grep '^+ '
   ```
   Anything added other than `"jsonschema>=4",` falsifies the fourth assumption.
4. **Are unknown kinds normalised?** Run this five-line test:
   ```python
   from code_facts.paths import FallbackEntry, normalise_kind  # names per D5
   for k in ["route", "", "ARGPARSE_SUBCOMMAND", "argparse", "model"]:
       print(repr(k), normalise_kind(k))
   ```
   Any output other than `other` for `route`, `""`, `argparse` and `model` falsifies the fifth assumption. The output for `ARGPARSE_SUBCOMMAND` shows whether matching is case-sensitive.
5. **Does the schema allow only the nine kinds?** Run:
   ```
   python -c "import json;from code_facts.paths import schema_text;print(sorted(set(json.dumps(json.loads(schema_text())).split('argparse_subcommand')[0:1])))"
   ```
   Or, more simply, check that the `EntryKind` `enum` array in `paths.v1.schema.json` has exactly 9 members. Any other count falsifies the fifth assumption.

Checking the code_facts pyproject and models to confirm "kind-rank" is an internal constant, not a package.## kind-rank

### What it is
`kind-rank` is not a third-party package. The dependency scanner matched the phrase "**Kind rank:**" in design.md § D3, which describes `KIND_RANK`, a module-level constant this change adds to `code_facts`. I checked three places. `https://pypi.org/pypi/kind-rank/json` and `https://pypi.org/pypi/kind_rank/json` both return **HTTP 404**. `code_facts/pyproject.toml` declares only `multiplai-core[sdk]` and `pydantic>=2`. A case-insensitive grep for `KIND_RANK|kind[-_]rank` across the installed `code_facts` package finds nothing. Today `code_facts/models.py` has one `Literal` (`Side = Literal["base", "head"]`) and no kind enum. This change will own and maintain `KIND_RANK` itself. Its job is to give each `EntryKind` a total precedence order. That order is used three times: to pick the winner when entries share a handler (D4 merge), to order entries before tracing under `trace_limit` (D10), and as the third tie-breaker in output path order (D10). No package should be added to `pyproject.toml` for it.

### The contract we rely on
No outside API exists. The contract is whatever the design promises, in its own words:

- D3: "`KIND_RANK` is the discovery precedence list, with `other` last." It is used for "merge precedence; pre-trace order; output ordering". "A test pins this ranking."
- The D3 enum, in declaration order: `argparse_subcommand, click_command, typer_command, main_module, project_script, skill_command, hook_command, seed, other`.
- The entry-point-discovery vocabulary, as D3 quotes it, puts two of these the other way round: `argparse_subcommand, click_command, typer_command, project_script, main_module, skill_command, hook_command, seed`.
- D4 merge: "Keep the entry with the smallest `(KIND_RANK, location.path, location.line)`. Move the others into `also_invoked_by`, sorted by `(path, line, kind)`."
- D4 output: "Entries are sorted by `(location.path, location.line, kind, name)`." This sorts by `kind`, not by `KIND_RANK`.
- D10 trace limit: "Reachable entries are ordered by `(distance, KIND_RANK, path, line)`."
- D10 path ordering: "`-len(covered)`, retained hop count, `KIND_RANK`, path, line."
- D5: model-fallback kinds outside the enum "become `other`" before any ranking happens.

The design does not define the constant's type (tuple, `dict[EntryKind, int]`, or derived from `list(EntryKind)`) or how a lookup is done.

### Edge cases & failure modes
- **Precedence order disagrees between specs (seen in the design text):** D3 declares `main_module` before `project_script`, but the discovery vocabulary D3 quotes lists `project_script` before `main_module`. Take a package whose `[project.scripts]` target is `pkg.__main__:main` and whose `__main__.py` calls `main()`. Both entries share a handler, so which one is kept and which goes to `also_invoked_by` depends only on this ordering. A test that "pins this ranking" will lock in whichever order was typed first, and the spec gives no tie-break.
- **A seed loses to a discovered entry at the same handler:** `seed` ranks eighth of nine. A caller who seeds a symbol that discovery also found will see the seed folded into `also_invoked_by`, and the kept entry has `source="discovered"`. The design says nothing about whether a seed should win. Unknown: is this intended? Check by asking the spec owner, and add a fixture that seeds an argparse handler.
- **Two different orders in the same output:** D4 sorts output entries and `also_invoked_by` by `kind`. If `EntryKind` is a `str`/`StrEnum`, that is alphabetical: `argparse_subcommand < click_command < hook_command < main_module < other < project_script < seed < skill_command < typer_command`. D10 sorts paths by `KIND_RANK`. Readers will see `hook_command` ahead of `skill_command` in one list and after it in the other. That is correct per spec, but it will look like a bug.
- **Empty or degenerate input:** an empty entry list sorts to `[]` and never looks up the constant. A one-member merge group looks it up once and cannot fail on a known kind. Nothing surprising here.
- **Malformed or unexpected-format input (a kind not in the table):** Python fails loudly, not quietly. `dict[...]` raises `KeyError`, and `tuple.index` raises `ValueError: tuple.index(x): x not in tuple`. Two paths can produce one: a fallback `kind` that slips past D5's "unknown → `other`" step, and a `str` read back from cached JSON (D7) compared against a plain `Enum` key. With `class EntryKind(str, Enum)` or `StrEnum`, `hash` and `==` match the raw string, so `{EntryKind.seed: 7}["seed"]` works. With a plain `Enum`, it raises `KeyError`.
- **Oversized input:** there are 9 kinds and lookups are O(1) or O(9). There is no limit, truncation or timeout. The one size-related risk is drift. If the constant is derived from `list(EntryKind)`, a new enum member shifts every later rank, and adding it after `other` breaks the "`other` last" rule without any error.
- **Concurrent or repeated use:** as a module global it is shared by every `bounded(concurrency)` task in `map_paths`. A `tuple` or `MappingProxyType` cannot be changed. A `list` or `dict` can be changed by a test or caller, and that change would carry over to later runs in the same process. It would also change merge results without changing the cache keys in D7, because the keys hash `(kind, location, handler)` and not the rank.
- **Offline / unavailable / unauthenticated:** not applicable at runtime, since there is no network, credentials or install step. The real risk is in packaging. The name `kind-rank` is **unclaimed on PyPI (404)**. If someone "fixes" the scanner warning by adding `kind-rank` to `dependencies`, `uv lock` fails today. If anyone later registers that name, it would install their code, which is a dependency-confusion opening.

### Assumptions we are making
- `KIND_RANK` gives a lower rank to `argparse_subcommand` than to `click_command`, and to every discovered kind than to `seed`, and `other` has the highest rank. A test that reads ranks for all nine `EntryKind` members gets distinct integers with `other` at the maximum.
- `KIND_RANK` covers every `EntryKind` member exactly once. `set(KIND_RANK) == set(EntryKind)` and `len(KIND_RANK) == len(EntryKind)`.
- Every entry reaching merge, trace-limit ordering or path ordering has a kind that is an `EntryKind` member. Looking up the rank of every entry and drop record from a run with an unknown-kind fallback answer raises no `KeyError` or `ValueError`.
- Looking up a rank with a raw JSON string (`"seed"`) gives the same result as looking it up with `EntryKind.seed`. That holds only if `EntryKind` subclasses `str`.
- The relative order of `main_module` and `project_script` is the one the discovery spec intends. The spec owner confirms which order is right, or a merge fixture with both kinds at one handler keeps the expected kind.
- Output entry order using `kind` (alphabetical) and path order using `KIND_RANK` are meant to differ. The spec owner confirms this, or one of them is changed.
- The constant cannot be changed at runtime. `KIND_RANK[...] = 0` (or `.append`) raises `TypeError` or `AttributeError`.

### How we would find out cheaply
Put this in `/tmp/kr_check.py` once `models.py`/`entries.py` exist and run `uv run python -I /tmp/kr_check.py` from `lib/code_facts`. Until then, paste a stand-in `EntryKind`/`KIND_RANK` at the top.

```python
from code_facts.entries import KIND_RANK; from code_facts.paths import EntryKind
rank = (lambda k: KIND_RANK[k]) if isinstance(KIND_RANK, dict) else KIND_RANK.index
assert set(KIND_RANK) == set(EntryKind) and len(KIND_RANK) == len(EntryKind)        # coverage
assert rank(EntryKind.other) == max(map(rank, EntryKind)) and rank(EntryKind.seed) == max(map(rank, EntryKind)) - 1
print("main_module<project_script:", rank(EntryKind.main_module) < rank(EntryKind.project_script))
print("raw str ok:", rank("seed") == rank(EntryKind.seed))                            # str-subclass check
try: KIND_RANK[0] = 1; print("MUTABLE")
except (TypeError, KeyError): print("immutable")
print(sorted(EntryKind) == sorted(EntryKind, key=rank))                               # alphabetical vs rank
```

What each result tells you:
- **Missing or duplicate kinds:** an `AssertionError` on line 3.
- **`other` not last, or `seed` not just before it:** an `AssertionError` on line 4.
- **`main_module` vs `project_script` order:** line 5 prints which way the table puts them, to compare with the discovery spec. If it prints `True`, the table follows D3's enum, not the quoted discovery vocabulary.
- **Raw strings fail:** a `KeyError`/`ValueError` on line 6, or `False`, means cached JSON kinds will break lookups.
- **Mutable constant:** `MUTABLE` means the "cannot be changed" assumption is wrong. If `KIND_RANK` is a dict, `KIND_RANK[0] = 1` can succeed and print `MUTABLE`. Use `MappingProxyType`.
- **Alphabetical vs rank:** `False` on the last line confirms the two orders differ, so the spec owner has to decide whether that is intended.

Last, run `uv lock` from a scratch copy with `"kind-rank"` added to `dependencies`. It should fail with "not found in the package registry", which confirms the name must never be added there.

## known-edges

### What it is
`known-edges` is not a third-party package, so it has no maintainer, no docs and no changelog. It is a term this design makes up. The dependency scanner flagged it because it saw the hyphenated phrase in design.md § Decisions. In D4 and D9, a "known edge" is a caller→callee line pair that discovery works out statically and stores on each `Entry.known_edges`. Examples are `args.func(...)` or a `set_defaults(func=…)` line pointing to the `def` line, a click decorator line pointing to its `def`, and a `SKILL.md` command line pointing to an argparse handler or `__main__.py:1`. The gate's rule 7 (`unconnected_hop`) uses these edges as one of three ways to accept that hop n+1 follows hop n. They are also part of the trace cache key and the `trace_entry` prompt. What I checked:
- `https://pypi.org/pypi/known-edges/json` returns HTTP 404. The npm page returned 403, so it is unverified but irrelevant to a Python library.
- Searching the whole multiplai marketplace tree for `known[-_ ]edges?` finds only one unrelated comment in `multiplai-context/scripts/lib/costing_collector.py:17` ("Known edge: if a collection pass runs…"). Nothing in `code_facts` or `walkthrough_pipeline` uses the term yet.

The scanner's "(0 declared name(s) scanned)" note is also wrong. `plugins/multiplai-dev/lib/code_facts/pyproject.toml` declares `multiplai-core[sdk]` and `pydantic>=2`, so the scanner probably read a different file. The real new runtime dependency in this change is `jsonschema>=4` (D13), and it needs its own explainer.

### The contract we rely on
No external API is called. The internal contract the design creates, as written in design.md:
- Producer: `discover_entries(root: Path, *, seeds: Sequence[Seed] = ()) -> Discovery`. Each `Entry` carries `known_edges`. When entries merge (D4), their edges are combined, duplicates removed and the list sorted ("Union the `known_edges` of the group, with duplicates removed and sorted").
- Consumer: `check_trace(hops, *, entry, edges, places, resolve, root) -> GateOutcome`. Rule 7 accepts hop n+1 if "there is a known edge from hop n's location to a line in hop n+1's range".
- Edge sources, per scanner (verbatim):
  - argparse: "from the `args.func(...)` or `HANDLERS[...](...)` call line when present, otherwise from the `set_defaults` line or dict entry line, to the `def` line"
  - click/typer: "decorator line to `def` line"
  - `SKILL.md`: "to the matching argparse subcommand's handler … otherwise to its `add_parser` line; otherwise to line 1 of `__main__.py`"
- Cache key (D7): "sorted applicable known edges and places" are part of the trace key.
- Existing code the edges sit next to:
  - `check_citation(citation: Citation, resolve: Resolve) -> str | None` (explore.py:74)
  - `async def ask(key, prompt, call, answers, *, call_kwargs, errors, recoverable=(Exception,), fatal=(), progress=None) -> None` (explore.py:109)
  - `Citation(_Model)`, with `line_start`/`line_end` typed `Field(ge=1)` (models.py:29)

The edge record's own type is **not defined anywhere** in the design: whether it holds a path, a line, a repo, or a range.

### Edge cases & failure modes
- **Empty / degenerate: entries with `handler=None` have no edges.** D4 says on purpose that in the `pr_pipeline` `args.command == "x"` case, `open`/`edit`/`render` keep `handler=None` and get no edge. Hop 1→2 for those entries can then only connect through a `NAME` token or a caller place. If hop 1 is the `add_parser("open")` line, the string `"open"` is a string token, not a `NAME`, so it does not match. Tracing those entries is likely to break at hop 2 every time (`unconnected_hop`), costing one re-ask and then a cut.
- **Empty / degenerate: non-Python hops connect only through edges.** D9 says `SKILL.md` and JSON hops "only connect through edges and places". A hook command whose target resolved to "line 1" of a file that isn't a module gets an edge to line 1. If the model's hop 2 cites the real function instead of line 1, nothing connects them.
- **Malformed input: the endpoint format is undefined.** "From hop n's location" does not say whether the edge's source line must equal `line_start`, fall anywhere in `[line_start, line_end]`, or match the cited quote line. A multi-line hop citing `args.func(args)` at lines 40–42, with the edge source at 41, passes or fails depending on that unwritten choice. Unknown: what the source-side match rule is. Check by writing the rule into D9 and adding a gate test where the hop range strictly contains the edge source.
- **Malformed input: cross-file and cross-repo edges.** The `SKILL.md` and hook edges point from a text file into a `.py` file, which may be in a different top-level repo of a multi-repo snapshot. It is unknown whether edge endpoints are snapshot-relative paths (the form the gate resolves with `resolve(path, "head")`) or repo-relative paths. Check by building a two-repo fixture whose `SKILL.md` invokes the other repo's module, then asserting the edge path starts with that repo's prefix.
- **Malformed input: line drift between discovery and the gate.** Edges come from `ast` line numbers of files on disk under `root`. The gate reads files through `git show <sha>:<rel>`. If the working tree differs from the commit `resolve` maps to (uncommitted edits, CRLF conversion), edge line numbers don't match the hop lines the gate checks. Unknown: whether `root` is guaranteed to equal the resolved sha. Check with a fixture that edits a file after commit, then compare `git show` with the edge line.
- **Oversized input: edges are unbounded.** There is no cap on edges per entry. After a merge, one shared handler such as a `main()` used by 30 subcommands collects every invoker's edges. All of them go into the prompt and the cache key. Unknown: how big the edge list gets on this repo's largest CLI. Check by running `discover_entries` on the repo root and printing `max(len(e.known_edges))`.
- **Oversized input: decorator stacks.** For a click/typer `def` with several decorators, Python 3.8+ `ast` reports `FunctionDef.lineno` as the `def` line, and each decorator node carries its own `lineno`. A "decorator line → def line" edge therefore spans several lines. Hop n has to include the decorator line itself, not only the `def`.
- **Concurrent / repeated use: "applicable" is undefined and sits in the cache key.** Edges are pure data, so they hold no thread state. But "sorted applicable known edges" in the trace key has no definition. If "applicable" ever depends on input order (for example, seeds merged in a different order changing which entry keeps an edge), the "Reordered inputs hit the cache" scenario breaks. D4 sorts seeds and edges, which should prevent this. That is an assumption, not something observed.
- **Concurrent / repeated use: merge changes the cache key.** Adding one new invoker to an existing handler changes that entry's combined edges, and with them its trace key. The next run then re-asks, and pays for, a trace that would otherwise have hit the cache.
- **Offline / unavailable / unauthenticated:** this doesn't apply. Edges come from purely local `ast`/`tomllib`/`json` parsing, with no network or credentials. The only "unavailable" case is a file that fails to parse. It then yields no entries and no edges (it becomes a `parse_error` diagnostic), so any chain through it can only connect by name tokens.

### Assumptions we are making
- `known-edges` is not a package to install. Disproved if any spec file names a PyPI/npm package `known-edges` or a `known_edges` import from outside the repo. Observed so far: PyPI returns 404 and the repo has no references.
- Every edge source line and target line falls within the snapshot file's line count at the `head` sha that `resolve` returns. Disproved by any edge whose target line exceeds the line count of `git show <sha>:<rel>`.
- An `ast` `FunctionDef.lineno` equals the line of the `def` keyword, not the first decorator, on Python ≥3.12 (the project's `requires-python`). Disproved if `ast.parse("@d\ndef f(): pass").body[0].lineno != 2`.
- Edge endpoints use the same snapshot-relative POSIX path form as `Citation.path`, so a plain string comparison in rule 7 is correct. Disproved by any edge path starting with `/`, `./`, or a path that is repo-relative and lacks the top-level repo directory.
- For the `pr_pipeline` shape, tracing still produces a path despite there being no edge. Disproved if the gate breaks at hop 2 with `unconnected_hop` on the fixture copy, for both the first answer and the re-ask.
- The combined edge list for any entry in this repo stays under about 50 items, so prompt size and cache keys stay small. Disproved by the discovery count below.
- Sorting edges gives the same order across runs and Python versions. Disproved if two runs with shuffled seeds produce different `json.dumps(sort_keys=True)` of `known_edges`.

### How we would find out cheaply
1. Confirm it is not a package (already done): `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://pypi.org/pypi/known-edges/json` printed `404`. Any `200` would disprove assumption 1.
2. Check the decorator line number:
   `uv run python -c 'import ast; n=ast.parse("@app.command()\n@opt\ndef f(): pass").body[0]; print(n.lineno, [d.lineno for d in n.decorator_list])'`
   The expected output is `3 [1, 2]`. Anything else disproves assumption 3.
3. Once `discover_entries` exists, run this five-line script from `plugins/multiplai-dev/lib/code_facts`:
   ```python
   from pathlib import Path; import subprocess, code_facts as cf
   root = Path("../../../..").resolve(); d = cf.discover_entries(root)
   print(max((len(e.known_edges) for e in d.entries), default=0))
   for e in d.entries:
       for ed in e.known_edges:
           n = len(subprocess.run(["git","-C",str(root),"show",f"HEAD:{ed.target.path}"],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout.splitlines())
           assert not ed.target.path.startswith(("/","./")) and ed.target.line <= n, ed
   ```
   - A max above about 50 disproves assumption 6.
   - Any assertion failure disproves assumption 2 or 4.
   - An `AttributeError` on `.target` means the edge type is still undefined. Write it into D4 before PR 1.
4. Run discovery twice with `seeds` shuffled. Diff `json.dumps([e.known_edges for e in d.entries], sort_keys=True, default=str)`. A non-empty diff disproves assumption 7.
5. Run the gate on the `pr_pipeline` fixture with a `FakeCall` that answers hop 1 at `add_parser("open")` and hop 2 at `cmd_open`'s `def`. Use `check_trace(..., edges=entry.known_edges, places=())`. If the result is `reason == "unconnected_hop"` with `broken_at == 2`, that disproves assumption 5. The design would then need either an edge from the `args.command == "open"` comparison or a documented acceptance that these entries get cut.

## line

### What it is
`line` is not a dependency of this change. The scanner picked up the word from `design.md § Decisions`, where it appears only as a field or concept name: `location.line`, `handler.line`, `line=None` on `parse_error` diagnostics, `line_start`/`line_end` on hops, `line_out_of_range`, `changed_lines`, `patch_line`, `invocation_line`. No decision imports, installs or calls anything called `line`. A package with that name does exist on PyPI, which is why this needs saying. Its metadata (`https://pypi.org/pypi/line/json`) shows `line` 0.8.2, summary "May the LINE be with you...", by Taehoon Kim (carpedm20). It is an unofficial client for the LINE messenger. Its last release was 2016-11-21, it declares no `requires_python`, and it has 39 releases in total. It has nothing to do with this change. What the change really depends on is the meaning of "line number" in the standard-library tools it uses: `ast`, `tokenize`, `str.splitlines`, `json`, `tomllib` and `git show`. Those tools disagree in a few places, and those disagreements are what this section covers.

### The contract we rely on
- **No `line` package API.** Nothing from the PyPI `line` package is used, and it must not be added to `pyproject.toml`. The only new runtime dependency D13 introduces is `jsonschema>=4`.
- **The line-number contract the design actually uses:**
  - `ast.parse(source, filename='<unknown>', mode='exec', *, type_comments=False, feature_version=None, optimize=-1)`: each node's `lineno` is 1-based and `end_lineno` is inclusive. Scanners use this for `location.line`, `handler.line` and the innermost enclosing `def`.
  - `tokenize.generate_tokens(readline)`: yields `TokenInfo(type, string, start, end, line)` with `start=(row, col)`, where `row` is 1-based. D9 rule 7 uses its `NAME` tokens.
  - `tomllib.loads(s, /, *, parse_float=float)` and `json.loads(s)` report no positions. The design's own line scans fill that gap (D4: the `[project.scripts]` key scan and the JSON-encoded command-string search).
  - Output models require `line ≥ 1` (D13). Diagnostics allow `line=None`. Coverage uses the inclusive range `[line_start, line_end]` (D10).

### Edge cases & failure modes
- **Wrong package name / install, observed on PyPI:** `uv add line` or `pip install line` would resolve to the 2016 carpedm20 LINE-messenger client, not anything about line numbers. If someone "fixes" this flagged item by declaring `line`, the lockfile gains an abandoned, unrelated package.
- **Empty or degenerate input:** `ast.parse("")` returns `Module(body=[], type_ignores=[])` and does not raise. An empty `.py` file therefore produces no entries and no diagnostic. It does not produce `parse_error`. An empty `SKILL.md` or `hooks.json` behaves differently: `json.loads("")` raises `JSONDecodeError` (a `ValueError`), which should become a `parse_error` diagnostic with `line=None`. `__main__.py` entries use "line 1" (D4) even when the file is empty, and then `line_out_of_range` (D9 rule 3) rejects any hop citing line 1 of a 0-line file.
- **Malformed or unexpected format: line-separator disagreement.** `ast` and `tokenize` treat only `\n`, `\r\n` and `\r` as line breaks. `str.splitlines()` also splits on `\v`, `\f`, `\x1c`–`\x1e`, `\x85`, `\u2028` and `\u2029`. If a file contains a form feed (common in older Python sources) or U+2028, line N from `ast` and line N from `text.splitlines()[N-1]` are different lines. That produces false `text_mismatch` or `line_out_of_range` failures in `check_trace`. Reading `git show` output must split the same way `ast` counts lines.
- **Malformed input: null bytes.** `ast.parse` on source containing `\x00` raises `ValueError("source code string cannot contain null bytes")` on Python ≤ 3.11 and `SyntaxError` on 3.12+. D4 catches only `SyntaxError` and `UnicodeDecodeError`, so on older interpreters one such file would crash discovery instead of giving `parse_error`.
- **Malformed input: partial fragments.** `tokenize.generate_tokens` over a cited fragment that ends inside an open bracket or triple-quoted string raises `tokenize.TokenError` ("EOF in multi-line statement/string"). D9 already plans a regex fallback for this. An unterminated single-line string is different: it raises `TokenError` on 3.12+, but on older versions it yields an `ERRORTOKEN` without raising. The fallback must therefore trigger on both.
- **Malformed input: JSON line search.** D4 finds a hook command's line by searching the raw text for `json.dumps(command)`. A file that writes the same string with different escapes misses that search, so no line is found. Examples: `\/`, `\u0024` for `$`, or raw non-ASCII where `json.dumps` defaults to `ensure_ascii=True`. Unknown: what fallback line is used on a miss? To check, write a fixture with `"command": "\u0024{CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/x.py"` and assert the diagnostic or line.
- **Oversized input:** Deeply nested expressions make `ast.parse` raise `SyntaxError: too many nested parentheses` (a tokenizer limit of 200 levels) or `RecursionError` / `MemoryError` during compilation. `RecursionError` and `MemoryError` are not in D4's catch list. Very long single-line files (minified or generated) give one huge "line", so a `check_quote` over it is costly but still correct. Unknown: is there a per-file size cap before `ast.parse`? To check, time `ast.parse` on a 50 MB generated module.
- **Concurrent or repeated use:** Line computations are pure and deterministic. `ast`, `tokenize` and `json` keep no shared state, and repeated parses of identical bytes give identical `lineno`s. The only shared state is D4's parse cache. Unknown: is the parse cache read from multiple threads during `run_tasks`? To check, grep the implementation for cache access from inside async tasks or the default executor.
- **Offline / unavailable / unauthenticated:** None of the line tools need network access. The phantom `line` package would need PyPI for `uv lock`, which is one more reason not to add it. `git show <sha>:<rel>` behaves differently, because it fails when the sha is missing from a shallow clone. That failure surfaces as `missing_file` (D9 rule 2), not as a network error.

### Assumptions we are making
- No module under `plugins/multiplai-dev/lib/code_facts/` will contain `import line` or `from line import`, and `pyproject.toml` / `uv.lock` will not list a package named `line`.
- `ast` `lineno`, `tokenize` `start[0]`, and the line index used by `check_trace` / `check_quote` on `git show` output refer to the same physical line for every file in the fixtures, including files containing `\f` or `\r\n`.
- Every `location.line` and `handler.line` that discovery emits is ≥ 1 and ≤ the file's line count as `ast` counts it.
- Catching `SyntaxError` and `UnicodeDecodeError` is enough to turn every unparseable `.py` file into a `parse_error` diagnostic on the project's minimum Python version.
- The JSON-encoded search string from D4 is found verbatim in every fixture `hooks.json` and `settings*.json`.

### How we would find out cheaply
```bash
# 1. Phantom dependency check: any output falsifies "no line package".
grep -RnE '^\s*(import|from)\s+line\b' plugins/multiplai-dev/lib/code_facts/ ; \
grep -nE '^\s*"?line[<>=~ "]' plugins/multiplai-dev/lib/code_facts/pyproject.toml plugins/multiplai-dev/lib/code_facts/uv.lock

# 2. Line-counting disagreement and parse-error types, run with the project's interpreter.
cd plugins/multiplai-dev/lib/code_facts && uv run python -I - <<'EOF'
import ast, sys
src = "x = 1\n\x0c\ndef f():\n    return 2\n" + "a = 1\u2028b = 2\n"
fn = next(n for n in ast.parse(src).body if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef))
print("ast def line", fn.lineno, "| splitlines says:", repr(src.splitlines()[fn.lineno-1]),
      "| split('\\n') says:", repr(src.split("\n")[fn.lineno-1]))
for bad in ["a\x00b", "(" * 300 + ")" * 300]:
    try: ast.parse(bad)
    except Exception as e: print(sys.version_info[:2], type(e).__name__, str(e)[:60])
EOF
```
How to read the results:
- Any match in step 1 falsifies the first assumption.
- In step 2, if `splitlines` prints anything other than `'def f():'`, the line-index assumption is falsified for `\f` / U+2028 files, and the gate must split with `"\n"` (after normalising `\r\n`).
- If the null-byte case prints `ValueError`, or the nesting case prints `RecursionError` / `MemoryError`, the "two exception types are enough" assumption is falsified.
- Last, add one hook fixture that writes the command with `\u0024`. If discovery reports no line, or a wrong line, for it, the JSON-search assumption is falsified.

I've checked the code. `line-out-of-range` isn't a package; it's the gate's rule-3 reason code. Writing the section now.

## line-out-of-range

### What it is
This is not a third-party dependency, so it doesn't belong in `pyproject.toml`. The scanner picked up a hyphenated spelling of `line_out_of_range`, which is reason code 3 of the new trace gate in design.md § D9 (`BreakReason` in `code_facts/gate.py`). It is our own code, maintained in this repo. Its job is to stop a model-produced trace at the first hop whose `line_start..line_end` falls outside the cited file at the `head` sha. Rule 2 (`missing_file`) runs before it and rule 4 (`text_mismatch`) after. Rule 3 rests on a real library underneath: the vendored `multiplai_core.citations` module (`file_at`, `lines_at`, `check_quote`), which D9 says rules 2–4 delegate to. That module's behaviour on out-of-range lines is the "real behaviour" that matters here, and it does **not** report out-of-range lines.

### The contract we rely on
All of the following is copied from `multiplai_core/citations.py` (the installed copy in `.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/multiplai_core/`) and `code_facts/explore.py`:

- `def file_at(repo: str, sha: str, path: str) -> str | None:` is decorated `@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=2048)`. It runs `git -c color.ui=never -c core.quotepath=off -C <repo> show <sha>:<path>`. Any non-zero exit returns `None`. Bytes that aren't UTF-8 are decoded with `errors="replace"`.
- `def lines_at(repo: str, sha: str, path: str, start: int, end: int) -> list[str] | None:` has this docstring: *"The text is split on `\n` the way git numbers lines. An *end* past the end of the file returns the lines that exist. A range that is not valid (*start* below 1, or *end* before *start*) returns `[]`."*
- `def check_quote(repo: str, sha: str, path: str, start: int, end: int, quote: str) -> str | None:` returns `None` on a pass. Otherwise it returns exactly one of `"empty quote"`, `"path not at commit"` or `"quote not at cited lines"`. It has **no out-of-range reason.**
- `def check_citation(citation: Citation, resolve: Resolve) -> str | None:` lives in `code_facts.explore`. It calls `resolve(citation.path, citation.side)` and passes the result to `check_quote`.
- Model bounds: `Hop` in `walkthrough_pipeline/models.py:122-128` has `line_start: int = Field(ge=1)` and `line_end: int = Field(ge=1)`, and **no** `end >= start` validator. `code_facts.Citation` has the same `ge=1` fields **plus** `_ordered`, which raises when `line_end < line_start`.
- What D9 promises on top of this: rule 3 fires after `missing_file` and before `text_mismatch`, and yields `broken_at=<hop index>`, `reason="line_out_of_range"` and one re-ask.

### Edge cases & failure modes
- **Empty or degenerate input (empty file):** `file_at` returns `""` for a zero-byte blob. `"".split("\n")` is `[""]`, so `lines_at(..., 1, 1)` returns `[""]` rather than signalling "no lines". A count based on `len(text.split("\n"))` would say an empty file has 1 line, and `1-1` would wrongly pass rule 3. It then fails rule 4 only because any non-empty quote misses.
- **Degenerate input (trailing newline):** `"a\nb\n".split("\n")` is `["a", "b", ""]`, which is 3 elements for a 2-line file. Counting lines that way accepts a cite of line 3 (one past EOF). Separately, `check_quote` on range `2-3` with quote `"b"` **passes**, because the phantom empty line is simply appended.
- **Range past end of file (the core surprise):** `lines_at` clamps silently, returning "the lines that exist". `check_quote(..., 18, 40, quote)` on a 21-line file passes if the quote is in lines 18–21. Delegating to `check_quote` alone therefore never yields `line_out_of_range`, and an inflated range is accepted as valid. Rule 3 needs its own line count, compared against `line_end`, done before the call. That count must use git's convention: `text.count("\n") + (not text.endswith("\n") and text != "")`. review-viewer already does this separately (`walkthrough.py:155-162`, `len(split_lines(...))`).
- **Malformed range (`line_end < line_start`):** if `TraceAnswer.Hop` copies the walkthrough `Hop` exactly, it has no ordering validator. A reversed range then parses, `lines_at` returns `[]`, and `check_quote` reports `"quote not at cited lines"`. That surfaces as `text_mismatch`, not `line_out_of_range`, unless rule 3 checks ordering itself. If the hop's citation is typed as `code_facts.Citation`, as D8 says, the same answer instead fails pydantic and becomes `malformed_answer` for the whole trace, before any hop rule runs.
- **Malformed range (`line_start=0` or negative):** `Field(ge=1)` rejects it at parse time in both models, so it becomes `malformed_answer` with `broken_at=1` and never reaches rule 3.
- **Malformed input (binary or non-UTF-8 file):** bytes are replaced with U+FFFD, not rejected. A binary blob gets a line count from its `\n` bytes, so rule 3 can pass on garbage. review-viewer special-cases this with `is_binary`; `multiplai_core` does not.
- **Oversized input (huge files, giant ranges):** `git show` reads the whole blob into memory with no timeout (`subprocess.run(..., check=False)` with no `timeout=`). A range like `1-1000000` on a large file is clamped silently, not refused. The 20-hop cap limits the number of hops, not the size of each range. The prompt says "keep the range short (1-15 lines)", but nothing enforces it.
- **Concurrent or repeated use:** `file_at` is a process-wide `lru_cache(maxsize=2048)` keyed by `(repo, sha, path)`. It is thread-safe for reads, but two simultaneous misses both run `git show`. Repeated checks of the same blob are free. Passing a moving ref such as `HEAD` instead of a sha caches stale text; the docstring warns about this. The gate is synchronous and runs inside `run_tasks` tasks, so a cold cache blocks the event loop for one `git` subprocess per new file.
- **Offline, unavailable or unauthenticated:** no network is involved. If `git` isn't on PATH, `subprocess.run` raises `FileNotFoundError`, which propagates rather than becoming `missing_file`. A bad repo path or an unknown sha gives exit 128, which becomes `None` and is reported as `missing_file` (rule 2). That hides "wrong sha passed by `resolve`" behind a model-blame reason. `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` stops git from prompting.
- **Unknown: whether `resolve` may return a sha whose blob is a submodule (gitlink) or a symlink.** `git show <sha>:<link>` prints the link target text as a 1-line file, so rule 3 counts 1 line. To check, commit a symlink in a fixture and call `lines_at` on it.

### Assumptions we are making
- `line_out_of_range` needs no new package. It is satisfied by stdlib plus the already-vendored `multiplai_core.citations`, so `uv lock` after this change shows no new entry for it.
- Rule 3 computes the line count itself. On a 21-line file, a hop citing `18-22` with a quote from line 18 yields `reason="line_out_of_range"`, **not** a pass and not `text_mismatch`.
- The line count matches git's: a file `"a\nb\n"` has 2 lines, so citing line 3 is out of range. A zero-byte file has 0 lines, so citing line 1 is out of range.
- A hop with `line_end < line_start` gets one consistent outcome, either `malformed_answer` at parse time or `line_out_of_range` at rule 3, and never `text_mismatch`.
- `line_start=0` never reaches rule 3, because pydantic rejects it as `malformed_answer` with `broken_at=1`.
- `check_quote`'s reason strings stay exactly `"empty quote"`, `"path not at commit"` and `"quote not at cited lines"`, because the gate maps them onto `missing_file` and `text_mismatch`.
- `resolve(path, "head")` always returns a full commit sha, not a ref, so the `lru_cache` never serves text from another commit.

### How we would find out cheaply
Run this from `plugins/multiplai-dev/lib/code_facts`, using `uv run python -I check.py` with the script in a scratch directory:

```python
import subprocess, tempfile, pathlib
from multiplai_core.citations import lines_at, check_quote
d = pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()); g = lambda *a: subprocess.run(["git","-C",d,*a],check=True,capture_output=True,text=True).stdout.strip()
g("init","-q"); (d/"a.py").write_text("a\nb\n"); (d/"e.py").write_text(""); g("add","."); g("-c","user.email=x@x","-c","user.name=x","commit","-qm","x"); sha=g("rev-parse","HEAD")
print(lines_at(str(d),sha,"a.py",2,3), check_quote(str(d),sha,"a.py",2,40,"b"))   # expect ['b',''] None  -> clamping confirmed
print(lines_at(str(d),sha,"e.py",1,1), lines_at(str(d),sha,"a.py",3,2))            # expect [''] []
```

What the output tells us:
- If the first line prints `['b', ''] None`, then `check_quote` alone can't detect out-of-range lines. That confirms rule 3 needs its own count. If it returned an error instead, the extra count would be redundant.
- If the second line prints `[''] []`, the empty-file and reversed-range behaviours above are confirmed.
- Then, against the real gate, call `check_trace` with a single hop `a.py:2-3` quote `"b"` and a single hop `e.py:1-1`. Any result other than `reason == "line_out_of_range"` disproves the git-convention-count assumption.
- Call it again with a hop `line_start=3, line_end=2`. If it returns `text_mismatch`, the reversed-range assumption is wrong.
- `uv lock --check` showing no new package confirms the first assumption.

## location

### What it is
`location` is not a third-party dependency. In design.md it is the name of a **field on this change's own Pydantic models**: `Entry.location` (where an entry point is declared, a `{path, line}` pair), and the `location.path` / `location.line` sort keys used for merge, drop and output ordering (D4, D9, D10, D11, D13). The scanner flagged it as new probably because the word appears in backticks in § Decisions ("Entries with `handler=None` group by identical `location`"). It found nothing in pyproject.toml either: the reason given says "0 declared name(s) scanned", so the scan probably didn't parse the manifest at all. That means the absence check proves nothing. There **is** a PyPI distribution called `location`, but it is unrelated. Its metadata, fetched from `https://pypi.org/pypi/location/json`: author "leo", summary "完善修复baidu接口" ("improve and fix the Baidu interface"), 7 releases from 0.0.1 to 0.0.7, the last on 2016‑09‑18, no description, no homepage, no `requires_python`. It is an abandoned wrapper around the Baidu geolocation API. Nothing in this change calls it or needs it. Its job in this change is **none**, and it must not be added to `pyproject.toml`. There is no maintainer to name: the field is part of the code_facts library this change adds, maintained by this team.

### The contract we rely on
No external API. What the change relies on is the shape of its own field, as written in design.md:

- Shape: `location` is an object with `path` (root-relative POSIX string) and `line` (int). D13: "path rules: the pattern `^(?!/)(?!.*(^|/)\.\.?(/|$))[^\\]+$` and `line ≥ 1`."
- Output models subclass `_Strict(_Model)` with `extra="forbid"`, so a `location` holding any key besides `path` and `line` fails validation.
- Merge (D4): "Group entries by `(handler.path, handler.line)`. Entries with `handler=None` group by identical `location`. Keep the entry with the smallest `(KIND_RANK, location.path, location.line)`."
- Output order (D4): "Entries are sorted by `(location.path, location.line, kind, name)`."
